message.content:
Read-only investigation in /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router + Prisma VPS hosting platform). Do NOT edit any file. I am writing internal documentation and need VERIFIED facts with real `file:line` citations (absolute paths, e.g. /opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts:40). Be very thorough. Flag anything simulated, stubbed, or written-but-never-read — this codebase has a known overclaiming problem.

Investigate the AUTH / RBAC / PLATFORM-FEATURES cluster:

1. Auth: `lib/auth.ts` — session cookies (name, signing, expiry), password hashing, login/register/reset flows (`app/login`, `app/register`, `app/forgot-password`, `app/reset-password`), impersonation (`impersonateUser`, `currentUser`, `realUser`).
2. 2FA: `lib/actions-2fa.ts`, `lib/totp-verify.ts`, `test/totp.test.ts`. CRITICAL — I must document why `lib/totp-verify.ts` is a PLAIN module (not `"use server"`) on purpose: exported from a `"use server"` file it became a publicly callable brute-force oracle. Verify this: read both files, check the top-of-file comments, confirm `totp-verify.ts` has NO `"use server"` directive, and find where it is imported. Quote the relevant comment lines. Also document the rate limiting on 2FA verification if any.
3. RBAC: `lib/rbac.ts`, `lib/admin-groups.ts` — the roles, the "areas" concept, `requireArea`, `requireAdmin`, staff roles (`lib/actions-staff.ts`, `app/admin/staff`), which admin pages guard which area. Enumerate the areas and the role→area mapping.
4. API tokens: `lib/actions-tokens.ts`, `lib/api-auth.ts`, `app/api/v1/**` — token format, hashing, scopes, what the public API actually exposes, rate limiting.
5. Teams / orgs: `lib/actions-teams.ts`, `app/dashboard/team`, `app/admin/orgs` — membership roles, invites, what a team member can actually do (is the permission check real or does it just list members?).
6. Support: `lib/actions-support.ts`, `lib/actions-chat.ts`, `app/dashboard/support`, `app/admin/support`, `app/admin/chat`, `app/api/chat/**` — tickets vs live chat, attachments, SLA fields, notifications.
7. Notifications: find the Notification model and its writers/readers, the bell in `components/portal/Shell.tsx`, email vs in-app.
8. Growth: `lib/growth.ts`, `lib/actions-growth.ts`, `lib/affiliate.ts`, `lib/actions-affiliate.ts`, `lib/promotions.ts`, `lib/actions-gift.ts`, `app/dashboard/refer`, `app/dashboard/affiliate`, `app/admin/coupons`, `app/admin/gift-codes`, `test/growth.test.ts`. What is real vs decorative.
9. Bandwidth: grep for bandwidth/traffic accounting — where is it measured, stored, enforced? Is there an actual overage charge or is it display-only?
10. Game servers: `lib/actions-games.ts`, `lib/actions-gameplans.ts`, `lib/game-config.ts`, `lib/actions-game-config.ts`, `worker/game-config.ts`, `worker/game-update.ts`, `app/dashboard/games`, `app/admin/games`, `app/admin/game-plans`, `test/games.test.ts`. Which games, how a game server is provisioned/configured, what the customer can change.
11. Build with AI: `lib/ai-build.ts` (61KB!), `lib/actions-claude.ts`, `lib/actions-claude-key.ts`, `lib/anthropic.ts`, `worker/claude.ts`, `app/dashboard/build`, `app/dashboard/claude-code`, `app/api/claude/**`. What it does end-to-end, where the API key is stored/encrypted (`lib/crypto-box.ts`), what runs on the VM.
12. Admin surfaces: list every `app/admin/*` page with a one-line description of what it does and which lib module backs it. Also `app/admin/jobs`, `app/admin/logs`, `app/admin/monitoring`, `app/admin/provisioning`, `app/admin/infrastructure`, `app/admin/improvements`, `app/admin/nodes`.
13. `lib/monitoring.ts`, `lib/analytics.ts`, `lib/log.ts`, `lib/rate-limit.ts`, `worker/monitor.ts`, `worker/abuse.ts`, `lib/actions-abuse.ts` — monitoring/alerting/abuse detection.
14. `lib/settings.ts` — the settings/feature-flag store. Enumerate every flag/key and its default, especially any flag gating "real" vs "simulated" infrastructure paths.

Report every citation as /opt/nxeon/path:line. Be concise per item but complete in coverage.

- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs").    213	/** Every entry across every section, in sidebar order. */
   214	export function adminEntries(): AdminEntry[] {
   215	  return ADMIN_NAV.flatMap((g) => g.entries);
   216	}
   217	
   218	/**
   219	 * Does `pathname` belong to `href`? Exact match, or a detail route beneath it
   220	 * (`/admin/users/123`). The bare "/admin" only ever matches exactly so it can
   221	 * never swallow every deeper route.
   222	 */
   223	export function hrefMatches(href: string, pathname: string): boolean {
   224	  if (pathname === href) return true;
   225	  if (href === "/admin") return false;
   226	  return pathname.startsWith(href + "/");
   227	}
   228	
   229	/**
   230	 * Resolve which top-level entry owns a given admin pathname, by longest
   231	 * matching member href. Returns null for admin paths outside the IA.
   232	 */
   233	export function entryForPath(pathname: string): AdminEntry | null {
   234	  let best: { entry: AdminEntry; len: number } | null = null;
   235	  for (const entry of adminEntries()) {
   236	    for (const tab of entry.tabs) {
   237	      if (hrefMatches(tab.href, pathname) && (!best || tab.href.length > best.len)) {
   238	        best = { entry, len: tab.href.length };
   239	      }
   240	    }
   241	  }
   242	  return best?.entry ?? null;
   243	}

   104	/** True-ish coercion for values stored as "true"/"false"/"on"/"1". */
   105	export function isTrue(v: string | undefined | null): boolean {

   107	}
   108	
   109	/** Read one setting, falling back to an explicit default then SETTINGS_DEFAULTS. */
   110	export async function getSetting(key: SettingKey | string, fallback?: string): Promise<string> {
   111	  const row = await db.setting.findUnique({ where: { key } });
   112	  if (row) return row.value;
   113	  return fallback ?? SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[key as SettingKey] ?? "";
   114	}

   116	/** Read one setting as a boolean. */
   117	export async function getSettingBool(key: SettingKey | string, fallback = false): Promise<boolean> {
   118	  const row = await db.setting.findUnique({ where: { key } });
   119	  if (row) return isTrue(row.value);
   120	  const def = SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[key as SettingKey];
   121	  return def !== undefined ? isTrue(def) : fallback;
   122	}

   124	/** Read one setting as an integer (cents, days, counts…). */
   125	export async function getSettingInt(key: SettingKey | string, fallback = 0): Promise<number> {
   126	  const raw = await getSetting(key, String(fallback));
   127	  const n = Number(raw);
   128	  return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : fallback;

   132	export async function setSetting(key: SettingKey | string, value: string): Promise<void> {

   142	 * ARE included — callers that hand this to the client (the settings page) must

   145	export async function getAllSettings(): Promise<Record<string, string>> {

   147	  const merged: Record<string, string> = { ...SETTINGS_DEFAULTS };
